name: iot-jobs-data
description: IoT Jobs is a service that allows you to define a set of jobs — remote operations that are sent to and executed on one or more devices connected to Amazon Web S…

subcommands.name: describe-job-execution
subcommands.description: Gets details of a job execution. Requires permission to access the DescribeJobExecution action

options.name: --job-id
options.description: The unique identifier assigned to this job when it was created

options.name: --thing-name
options.description: The thing name associated with the device the job execution is running on

options.name: --include-job-document
options.description: Optional. Unless set to false, the response contains the job document. The default is true

options.name: --no-include-job-document
options.description: Optional. Unless set to false, the response contains the job document. The default is true

options.name: --execution-number
options.description: Optional. A number that identifies a particular job execution on a particular device. If not specified, the latest job execution is returned

options.name: --cli-input-json
options.description: Performs service operation based on the JSON string provided. The JSON string follows the format provided by ``--generate-cli-skeleton``.

options.name: --generate-cli-skeleton

subcommands.name: start-command-execution
subcommands.description: Using the command created with the CreateCommand API, start a command execution on a specific device

options.name: --target-arn
options.description: The Amazon Resource Number (ARN) of the device where the command execution is occurring

options.name: --command-arn
options.description: The Amazon Resource Number (ARN) of the command. For example, arn:aws:iot:<region>:<accountid>:command/<commandName>

options.name: --parameters
options.description: A list of parameters that are required by the StartCommandExecution API when performing the command on a device

options.name: --execution-timeout-seconds
options.description: Specifies the amount of time in second the device has to finish the command execution. A timer is started as soon as the command execution is created.

options.name: --client-token
options.description: The client token is used to implement idempotency. It ensures that the request completes no more than one time.

subcommands.name: update-job-execution
subcommands.description: Updates the status of a job execution. Requires permission to access the UpdateJobExecution action

options.name: --job-id
options.description: The unique identifier assigned to this job when it was created

options.name: --thing-name
options.description: The name of the thing associated with the device

options.name: --status
options.description: The new status for the job execution (IN_PROGRESS, FAILED, SUCCESS, or REJECTED). This must be specified on every update

options.name: --status-details
options.description: Optional. A collection of name/value pairs that describe the status of the job execution. If not specified, the statusDetails are unchanged.

options.name: --step-timeout-in-minutes
options.description: Specifies the amount of time this device has to finish execution of this job.

options.name: --expected-version
options.description: Optional. The expected current version of the job execution. Each time you update the job execution, its version is incremented.

options.name: --include-job-execution-state
options.description: Optional. When included and set to true, the response contains the JobExecutionState data. The default is false

options.name: --no-include-job-execution-state
options.description: Optional. When included and set to true, the response contains the JobExecutionState data. The default is false

options.name: --include-job-document
options.description: Optional. When set to true, the response contains the job document. The default is false
